description: Consumer checks for ZIP-bomb protection (SPEC Section 13.1; test T-018): archives whose declared sizes lie, whose compression ratio is extreme, or whose entries share data to fake a huge total. The archives are generated by tools/build-zip-fixtures.py and are each under 80 KB. Section 13.1 makes limits a SHOULD; first-party MDZip core libraries treat these cases as MUST. A consumer's limits may be configurable and may differ from each other, but its defaults must be no looser than referenceLimits for these cases to apply; stricter defaults pass too. Each case lists the outcomes that pass; anything else fails. In every case, a consumer that opens the archive must still read index.md normally.

referenceLimits.note: maxEntries is not exercised by an archive here: exceeding it needs ZIP64 and a multi-megabyte file. Test it with a configured lower limit if the consumer supports one.

pass: Reject the archive at open with ERR_ZIP_INVALID or ERR_LIMIT_EXCEEDED.
Open the archive, then fail reading or extracting data/blob.bin with ERR_ZIP_INVALID or ERR_LIMIT_EXCEEDED, having decompressed little more than the declared 1024 bytes.
fail: Returning more than 1024 bytes for data/blob.bin.
Returning the first 1024 bytes as if the entry were intact.
Failing with an error that has no stable code (for example the ZIP library's own exception).

pass: Reject the archive at open with ERR_LIMIT_EXCEEDED.
Open the archive, then fail reading or extracting data/zeros.bin with ERR_LIMIT_EXCEEDED before producing its 64 MiB.
fail: Returning or extracting the 64 MiB of data/zeros.bin.

cases.entries: data/part-000.bin to data/part-299.bin (300 central directory entries sharing one 16 MiB DEFLATE stream; only data/part-000.bin has a matching local header)
pass: Reject the archive at open with ERR_LIMIT_EXCEEDED (declared total over maxTotalUncompressedBytes).
Reject the archive at open with ERR_ZIP_INVALID (entries sharing data, or central directory names that don't match their local headers).
fail: Opening the archive and reading the listed entries one after another, decompressing far more than the file contains.
Opening the archive while listing fewer entries than its central directory, with no error: the central directory governs (Section 4).
